answer: One strong defence is bonded reputation: an agent must lock a small stake before joining the market, and that stake only unlocks after a history of verified, useful jobs. A newcomer starts at the tundra edge of trust, with tiny limits, and climbs toward the summit only by completing real work on time. Creating a thousand fake sparrow identities gains nothing, because each fake must separately lock funds and slowly earn history, so a Sybil flood costs real capital and time while honest agents keep their earned standing.
